# $crav1-explain-existing-system

lane: cross-cutting | group: Keep the picture current | starter: no | stage: stable | since: 1.8.0 | prompts: 0
purpose: Read the system notes spark, ideas, intake, match, or existing-to-specs already wrote (docs/system/).
use_when: System notes already exist
reads: Reads the `docs/system/` notes spark, ideas, intake, or match already wrote, and on every run the feature index against each slice’s node in `docs/system/diagrams.md` and its line in `## How the parts connect`.
writes: Writes a short TLDR in the chat, one level deeper only when asked, one part when pointed at, and, when the picture has nothing on the question, the first paragraph of the matching spec labelled as coming from the spec. Shows a stale research note as stale.
leaves alone: Leaves specs, code, and the picture alone.
limits: does not guess, invent a second document, teach, or start Specify, Plan, or Build. Names match only by slug, spec title, or main resource name. At the end it lists each slice missing entirely or partly, including done and retired, with status, and names `$crav1-refresh-system-notes` without running it. When no spec matches either, it says so and names `$crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this` without running it. It does not clear a stale research mark.
flow:
- When system notes already exist, **`$crav1-explain-existing-system`** reads `docs/system/` and answers with a short TLDR.
- On every run it compares the feature index with each slice's diagram node and its line under `## How the parts connect`.
- It lists each slice missing entirely or partly, including done and retired, with status, and names `$crav1-refresh-system-notes`.
- When the picture has nothing on the question, it quotes the first paragraph of the matching spec, labelled as coming from the spec, and names `$crav1-what-do-we-know-about-this`.
- Reads `docs/system/`.
